nodes.name: Hydrothermal synthesis of (Ni3Fe-FeV2O4)@C/NF
nodes.procedure: Fe(NO3)3·9H2O (262 mg), Ni(NO3)2·6H2O (141 mg), NH4VO3 (59 mg), and urea (130 mg) were added into a mixed solution (15 mL of deionized water and 15 mL of ethylene glycol). After magnetic stirring for 15 min, the solution and the pretreated NF were put into a 50 mL autoclave lined with Teflon at 160 °C for 12 h. After cooling down, the NF was rinsed in ethanol and deionized water, respectively. After vacuum drying, it annealed in a tube furnace at 450 °C for 2 h under a continuous flow of 5% H2 and 95% Ar atmosphere.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM image shows ultrasmall nanoparticles evenly distributed on mesoporous nanosheets of the catalyst.
nodes.evidence_snippet: After annealing, ultrasmall nanoparticles are evenly distributed on the mesoporous nanosheets (Figure S1b), which is confirmed by the TEM image in Figure S3.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows lattice fringes of 0.205 nm (Ni₃Fe(111)) and 0.253 nm (FeV₂O₄(311)), obvious interface between Ni₃Fe and FeV₂O₄, and numerous mesopores.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In Figure 2b, the lattice fringes of 0.205 and 0.253 nm can be observed, corresponding to the XRD results of Ni₃Fe(111) and FeV₂O₄(311), respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM confirms crystal structure with lattice fringes, single carbon layer, and mesoporous structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: TEM and high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) are used to further analyze the crystal structure.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS mappings reveal uniform distribution of Fe, Ni, V, C, and O elements on the surface of nanosheets.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The energy dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) mappings reveal the uniform distribution of Fe, Ni, V, C, and O elements on the surface of nanosheets (Figure 2f-j).

nodes.characterization_summary: BET analysis shows surface area of 158.05 m²/g, pore volume of 0.28 cm³/g, and average pore size of 7.03 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure S5 and Table S1, the surface area (158.05 m²g⁻¹) and the pore volume (0.28 cm³g⁻¹) of (Ni₃Fe-FeV₂O₄)@C/NF are much larger than those of others.
Peaks at 44.2°(111), 51.5°(200), and 75.8°(220) are attributed to Ni₃Fe(PDF#88-1715), while others at 29.9°(220), 35.3°(311), 56.7°(511), and 62.3°(440) are assigned to FeV₂O₄(PDF#75-1519).

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows Fe 2p peaks at 705.6/724.2 eV (Fe⁰), 711.7/730.4 eV (Fe²⁺), 715.2/733.9 eV (Fe³⁺); Ni 2p at 852.7/869.6 eV (Ni⁰), 855.9/873.8 eV (Ni²⁺); V 2p at 515.8/523.1 eV (V³⁺), 516.9/524.5 eV (V⁴⁺); O 1s at 529.9 eV (metal oxide), 531.2 eV (lattice oxide), 532.2 eV (chemisorbed oxide); C 1s at 284.8 eV (C-C), 286.1 eV (C-N), 289.3 eV (C=O).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 3b–f exhibits Fe 2p, Ni 2p, V 2p, O 1s, and C 1s of (Ni₃Fe-FeV₂O₄)@C/NF. The peaks at 705.6, 711.7, and 715.2 eV belong to Fe⁰ 2p₃/₂, Fe²⁺ 2p₃/₂, and Fe³⁺ 2p₃/₂, respectively...

nodes.characterization_summary: ICPMS used to investigate metal content of powders collected from NF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICPMS, Agilent ICPMS 7500CE) was used to investigate the metal content.
